name: omnisense/omnical
description: Omnical: calendars and public holidays under any PHP host, whoever keeps them - a user's calendars and their events read and written (time zones, recurrence kept as RRULE data, attendees and their answers, ETags against lost updates), busy time and the free spans everyone shares, a country's public and school holidays by region and type. One family in three contracts: calendar-events, free-busy, holidays. Providers are packages of their own (omnical/google, omnical/microsoft, omnical/caldav in code; omnical/openholidays, omnical/nager as data: a provider described by a definition file, loaded at run time with no class of its own), each declaring its usage policy, enforced on every call and tightened by a site's configuration - on omnisense/contracts. OAuth 2.0 (authorization code, PKCE, refresh) and secrets by reference included.

suggest.omnical/google: Google Calendar (API v3): calendars, events read and written, free/busy, over OAuth 2.0
suggest.omnical/microsoft: Microsoft Graph: Outlook and Microsoft 365 calendars, events read and written, schedules (free/busy), over OAuth 2.0
suggest.omnical/caldav: CalDAV (RFC 4791): iCloud, Fastmail, Nextcloud, any sabre/dav server - calendars, events read and written, free/busy
suggest.omnical/openholidays: OpenHolidays API: public and school holidays of 36 countries by region, no key, open data (ODbL) - a declared provider
suggest.omnical/nager: Nager.Date: public holidays of 200+ countries, no key (commercial use needs a sponsorship) - a declared provider
suggest.symfony/http-client: The HTTP client a declared provider uses when none is given
suggest.symfony/yaml: Provider definitions written in YAML (JSON needs nothing)
suggest.omnisense/omnibridge: The host contracts; omnibridge/symfony and omnibridge/laravel wire omnical into their host when a site needs it
